quote: Yeah. No. There's not a pocket cost during upfront fees.
stewart_read: Customer surfaced a strong belief (no out-of-pocket cost, bank-backed installs) originating from a friend's secondhand account. Rather than flip this into bill-pain framing or clarify precisely what 'no cost' means, the rep just confirms the claim flatly and moves on, leaving an unanchored belief that could become a credibility problem at the closer stage.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged that clarifying now risked deflating the customer's enthusiasm before qualification was complete — a strategic deferral to the closer. But nothing in the transcript shows the rep planning to loop back, so this reads as an omission rather than a deliberate sequencing choice.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to briefly clarify what 'no cost' actually means (financing structure, not free product) before the customer carries an inflated expectation into the closer call — cheap to fix now, costly to unwind later.

quote: Do you know how much you're kinda paying on average per month with them?
stewart_read: Rep asks the anchor question directly and gets a real range ($70 summer, over $150 winter) but only acknowledges the seasonal swing mechanically rather than using it to reinforce urgency or align emotionally against the utility.
coaching_implication: See bill_anchor_audit — flip was never executed. Coach the rep to use the seasonal doubling as a concrete pain point when transitioning to bill collection or scheduling.

quote: And do you guys come out and inspect, like, the roof and everything and make sure that's in a good condition before you do any install?
stewart_read: Customer voluntarily asks a forward-looking process question about install prep — a sign he is already picturing the installation happening, not just evaluating whether to proceed. This is a buying-temperature signal the rep should log for the closer.
coaching_implication: Rep answered adequately ('100%... we do a site survey') but didn't flag this enthusiasm for the handoff. Manager should note this as a signal the closer can lean into early.

quote: Do you wanna go down, for each each month reading off each number to me?
stewart_read: The customer was already logged into his online utility account and had just volunteered a usable summary ('anywhere from 200 to 600 kilowatts,' plus two specific monthly figures). Instead of taking that shortcut or asking for a screenshot/text, the rep defaulted to a full 12-month verbal read-aloud — the slowest path in the schema's bill_collection guidance, burning nearly two minutes on numbers a text photo could have captured in seconds.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive default to the most thorough script option rather than a deliberate efficiency call — there's no evidence the rep considered the faster text/photo alternative once online access was confirmed.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to recognize when a customer is already logged in as the cue to request a screenshot or photo text instead of a verbal readout — this is a repeatable time-burn pattern worth flagging per bill_collection.alternative_paths.shopping_customer_protocol logic even though this customer was at home, not shopping.

stewart_read: Transcription/diarization artifact: the customer's spoken dollar figures ($199, $198, etc.) are being rendered by Deepgram as date-formatted strings, and the rep has to stop and ask for a repeat. This is a transcription quality issue, not a rep error, but it explains why the bill readout took longer than it should have.
coaching_implication: No coaching action needed on the rep; flag for QA that this transcript segment has garbled numeric formatting so the manager doesn't misread the pacing as the rep's fault.

stewart_read: Customer disclosed a prior solar design about a year ago but the rep's own line here is a garbled transcription fragment, and no follow-up probe (which company, what was shown, why it didn't move forward) occurs. This is free competitive intelligence the closer will want.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have been satisfied that the timing (a year ago) meant the prior design was stale and irrelevant, choosing not to spend time on it. But no reasoning is stated, so the omission reads as unprobed rather than deliberately dismissed.
coaching_implication: Coach a 10-second follow-up next time: which company, and why didn't it happen — this context is cheap to gather and useful for the closer's positioning.

stewart_read: Rep locks day and time and sends a reminder text promise, but never runs the full button-up handshake — no one-hour block statement, no 'don't be driving, be at your computer' framing, and no explicit 'is that fair?' confirmation.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to add the no-driving/computer expectation and the explicit fairness check before ending calls — these are the mechanics most correlated with show rate per button_up guidance.
